how_verified: Read server/internal/handler/http.go, middleware.go, access.go, routes.go in full (not diff-only) and confirmed handleUsers no longer reads userID from parts[0]/URL; owner comes exclusively from requireIdentity(w,r) which sources Identity from request context populated by RequireAuth.

Wrote an independent httptest-based probe file (not copied from the implementer's or Task 5's suite) against the real handler.BuildRoutes wiring, using two distinct fixture users (ivanov/petrov) with seeded cross-owner data, covering: (a) stray/legacy URL segment where {userID} used to be, including on the settings endpoint (not just chats, which the implementer's suite already covers), asserting on response BODY content (a foreign labor_minute_rate marker), not just status code; (b) foreign user_id field in JSON body on POST /api/v1/users/settings (implementer's suite only covered POST chats) — rejected, petrov's settings unchanged; (c) foreign user_id in query string on GET routes; (d) foreign chat ID on RESTORE specifically (implementer's suite covers DELETE and calculate explicitly but not a dedicated negative restore case) — 404, and petrov's soft-deleted chat was NOT restored by ivanov's request.

Ran the full server/internal/handler test package (implementer's suite + my own probes) 8 times in a row (go test -count=1, both filtered and full package) via the specified docker golang:1.25-alpine command against the real MariaDB-backed build — all runs after the first were 100% green, including every US-15/US-16 negative case.

Independently probed requireIdentity as a Go unit (not just via HTTP) with (i) no Identity at all in context and (ii) a zero-value Identity{} explicitly stored in context — both fail closed with 401 and an empty returned login, confirming the fail-closed guarantee holds even under a hypothetical wiring bug that skips RequireAuth.

Read server/internal/repository/postgres.go DeleteChat/RestoreChat: both scope their SQL with 'WHERE user_id = ? AND id = ?' using the session-derived userID, and ensureAffected() returns service.ErrNotFound when 0 rows match — i.e. ownership is enforced at the SQL layer independent of the handler, confirmed by direct code read plus a live probe against the real PostgresRepository via TEST_DB_DSN (go test ./internal/repository/... passed against the running MariaDB instance).
Confirmed POST /auth/yandex still 404s (existing test TestBuildRoutes_LegacyYandexTokenRouteIsGone, re-run and passing) and no other Task 5 finding regressed.
go build ./... succeeds; go test ./internal/handler/... and ./internal/service/... and ./internal/repository/... (against live MariaDB) all pass with no regressions.

transient_anomaly_note: The very first test invocation of my probe suite (before any code changes) failed nearly every US-15/US-16 case in a pattern that looked exactly like the OLD pre-fix routing logic (owner taken from URL). This was alarming enough to investigate directly: I diffed the on-disk http.go against the container's mounted copy (byte-identical, unambiguously the fixed version), added temporary diagnostic logging, and re-ran — every subsequent run (8 total, including the exact original command with no code changes) passed cleanly and consistently. I attribute the one anomalous run to a transient Docker/WSL2 bind-mount read glitch rather than a real code defect: the source is deterministic (no goroutines, no randomness in this request path) and has been stable across 8 repeat runs since. Flagging this transparently rather than silently omitting it, but it does not change the verdict — the fix is real and consistently enforced.
clean_check: N/A - findings present (see below), but full-coverage checks performed: A01 Broken Access Control (primary focus — IDOR closure, see verdict above; RequireAuth/RequireAccess/RequireAdmin chain order verified in routes.go; RequireSameOrigin CSRF protection on mutating routes re-verified via existing passing tests), A02 Cryptographic Failures (not in scope of this diff — no crypto/secret handling touched by Task 6), A03 Injection (no new SQL construction in this diff; DisallowUnknownFields on decodeJSON re-confirmed to reject a foreign user_id field with 400 on both /chats and /settings), A04 Insecure Design (see finding 2), A05 Security Misconfiguration (no config/header changes in this diff), A06 Vulnerable Components (no dependency changes in this diff), A07 Auth Failures (requireIdentity fail-closed re-verified directly, see verdict), A08 Software/Data Integrity (no deserialization changes beyond existing DisallowUnknownFields, no CI/CD changes), A09 Logging and Monitoring (see finding 1 — this is where the actual gap is: no regression alarm if repository-layer ownership scoping regresses), A10 SSRF (not applicable, no outbound URL construction from user input in this diff). Hardcoded-secrets scan: grepped the five changed files for API_KEY=/SECRET=/PASSWORD=/TOKEN=/connection-string patterns and inspected every literal string — none found; the only credential-shaped string in the touched files is the openapi.yaml/test fixture's illustrative 'dsn=poshivon:poshivon@tcp(db:3306)' constant in http_test.go, which is explicitly a synthetic fixture asserting that such text must NEVER appear in a real response (TestWriteAPIDomainError_NoInternalTextInAnyBranch), not a real secret.

findings.category: A09: Security Logging and Monitoring / best-practice
findings.title: No repository-contract regression test protects DeleteChat/RestoreChat ownership scoping in production (Postgres) or Memory repositories
findings.description: PostgresRepository.DeleteChat/RestoreChat (server/internal/repository/postgres.go:339-373) correctly scope every UPDATE/DELETE by 'WHERE user_id = ? AND id = ?' using the session-derived owner, and MemoryRepository.DeleteChat/RestoreChat (server/internal/repository/memory.go:109-153) correctly index by the per-user map. Both are currently correct. However, server/internal/repository/access_repo_test.go (Task 3's repository contract suite) contains zero test cases exercising DeleteChat or RestoreChat at all, let alone a cross-user case (grep for 'DeleteChat|RestoreChat' in that file returns no hits). The only place this invariant is currently exercised is server/internal/handler/http_test.go's TestHandleUsers_ForeignOwnerUnreachable — a handler-level integration test, not the repository-layer contract suite that both PostgresRepository and MemoryRepository are supposed to satisfy identically. This is exactly the implementer's self-disclosed gap: a mutation that broke owner-scoping in MemoryRepository.DeleteChat during development was caught only by the handler test. If a future change to postgres.go's WHERE clause (e.g. during a refactor, an ORM upgrade, or a query builder change) silently drops the user_id predicate, nothing in the repository package's own test suite would catch it — only the handler-level integration test would, and that test could be skipped, disabled, or miss a specific mutation shape.
findings.location: server/internal/repository/access_repo_test.go (missing coverage); server/internal/repository/postgres.go:339-373 and server/internal/repository/memory.go:109-153 (the currently-correct code this should protect)
findings.impact: If repository-layer ownership scoping regresses in a future change, the regression would only be caught by handler-level tests (or not at all, if that specific request shape isn't covered there) rather than by the repository contract suite whose explicit job is to verify this invariant per-implementation. This re-opens the exact class of bug this task was built to close, with a longer detection lag.
findings.recommendation: Add cross-user DeleteChat/RestoreChat cases to server/internal/repository/access_repo_test.go (or a sibling costing_repo_test.go run against both PostgresRepository and MemoryRepository as a shared contract, mirroring how the settings/chat contract tests are structured): seed a chat under owner A, attempt DeleteChat/RestoreChat with owner B's login and A's chatID, assert ErrNotFound and that A's chat is unaffected. Run the same table-driven case against both repository implementations so a regression in either backend fails at the repository layer, not just the handler layer.
findings.cwe: CWE-1173 (Improper Use of Validation Framework) / not directly applicable — this is a test-coverage gap, not an active vulnerability

findings.title: CalculateInChat does not explicitly verify chat ownership/existence before computing; relies solely on a DB foreign-key constraint
findings.description: service.CostingService.CalculateInChat (server/internal/service/costing.go:411-580) never calls a GetChat/ownership check before running the pricing calculation and calling calcRepo.AppendCalculation(ctx, result) with the caller-supplied chatID. In production this is saved from being an integrity hole only by the composite foreign key 'calculations.(user_id, chat_id) REFERENCES chats(user_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE' (server/migrations/002_costing_schema.up.sql:45) — a POST .../calculate against a nonexistent or foreign chatID under the caller's own session-scoped userID will fail the INSERT with a raw FK-violation error from GORM, which classifyDomainError (server/internal/handler/http.go:286-314) has no sentinel for and therefore surfaces as a generic 500 'internal_error' rather than a clean 404 'not_found'. This is NOT a cross-user data leak (userID is always session-derived post-Task-6, so the write always lands in the caller's own space) and is fail-closed (DB rejects the insert), but it is a defense-in-depth gap: the service layer does the same full pricing computation and settings lookup before failing, and the failure mode is an opaque 500 instead of an explicit 404 the client could act on. This behavior predates Task 6 (chatID handling itself wasn't touched by this task beyond the index shift) but is directly relevant to point 4 of this audit (whether ownership is verified before acting on a chat, independent of the handler).
findings.location: server/internal/service/costing.go:411-580 (CalculateInChat); server/internal/handler/http.go:164-199 (handleCalculate, unchanged call site); server/migrations/002_costing_schema.up.sql:45 (the FK that currently saves this)
findings.impact: Low as a security issue (fail-closed, no cross-user exposure) but a minor robustness/UX gap: a legitimate client error (referencing a deleted/nonexistent/foreign chat ID) is reported as an opaque server error (500) rather than a clean 404, and the server does unnecessary work (a full pricing calculation and settings fetch) before the DB rejects the write.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit chat-ownership check (e.g. a lightweight GetChat(ctx, userID, chatID) or ExistsChat call) at the top of CalculateInChat, returning service.ErrNotFound before running the calculation, so the 404 is intentional and the FK constraint becomes a defense-in-depth backstop rather than the only enforcement mechanism. Low priority — track separately from Task 6's IDOR closure since it's pre-existing and not exploitable cross-user.
findings.cwe: CWE-754 (Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions)
